assigned.title: This artist is dominating AI-generated art. And he’s not happy about it.
assigned.author: Melissa Heikkilä
assigned.task: Read the article (about 10 minutes). Connect it to the “memorized style” slides.
assigned.summary: Greg Rutkowski is a Polish illustrator known for fantasy landscapes painted in a classical style. His name was used as a prompt about 93,000 times with Stable Diffusion, far more than famous names such as Picasso. At first he thought it might bring him new viewers; then he found AI images carrying his name that he never made, and worried that his real work would become hard to find.
prompts: Why did so many people type Rutkowski's name into their prompts?
What exactly worries him: copying, credit, income, or something else?
Is using an artist's name in a prompt homage, mimicry, or something new?
assigned.connection: Tonight's slides showed Stable Diffusion imitating his style, and then a model that was made to forget it.
assigned.note: This is a news report from 2022. The legal cases and the tools have changed since.

assigned.title: Ablating Concepts in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
assigned.author: Nupur Kumari, Bingliang Zhang, Sheng-Yu Wang, Eli Shechtman, Richard Zhang, and Jun-Yan Zhu
assigned.task: Read the abstract on the project page and look closely at the before-and-after figures. You do not need to read the method.
assigned.summary: The paper shows how to make a text-to-image model “forget” one thing — a living artist's style, a copyrighted character, or a memorized photo — while keeping everything else. Ask for Grumpy Cat and you get an ordinary cat; ask for a painting in Greg Rutkowski's style and the style is gone.
prompts: Pick one before-and-after pair. What exactly changed?
Who should decide what a model is made to forget?
Does removing an artist's name from one model protect the artist?
assigned.connection: This is the method behind tonight's R2D2, Snoopy, Van Gogh and Greg Rutkowski slides.
assigned.note: The equations are optional. The figures are the reading.

assigned.title: Multi-Concept Customization of Text-to-Image Diffusion (Custom Diffusion)
assigned.author: Nupur Kumari, Bingliang Zhang, Richard Zhang, Eli Shechtman, and Jun-Yan Zhu
assigned.task: Read the abstract on the project page and look at the results. Compare Custom Diffusion with DreamBooth and Textual Inversion.
assigned.summary: Custom Diffusion teaches a model a new concept — a pet, an object, a style — from only a few photos, by changing just a small part of the model and adding a new word such as “V* dog”. Because the change is small, two separately learned concepts can be combined in one image.
prompts: How many images does the model need to learn a new concept?
What is the new word V* for?
Which example would be most useful for your own film?
assigned.connection: Most of tonight's customization slides — the moongate, Jun-Yan's dog, the wooden pot — come from this paper.
assigned.note: You are not expected to understand the optimization.
